claim: H1 (low-then-high / feedforward) vs H2 (high-then-low / feedback) vs H3 (superposition / near-simultaneous, e.g. volume conduction) test of spiking-onset latency across the 10-area hierarchy (figstyle.AREA_ORDER), per response class (omnibus, S+, S-, O+, O-). Pipeline: jnwb/onset_fitting.py (causal forward-only exponential PSTH smoothing, tau=30ms; causality-bounded exponential onset fit, t0 in [0, window_end] by construction) + scripts/fit_class_onset_latency.py (per-session per-area per-class extraction, session-level bootstrap CI, Spearman rank-vs-onset permutation test, Holm/BH correction across the 5 classes). Both files built 2026-08-15 in a concurrent session (not this one) for Hamm's request relayed via Andre (PI): test whether omission-responsive units combine O+/O++ (structurally a no-op -- O++ is already a strict subset of O+ in omission_grand_units.csv's classification), and whether cross-area onset timing supports feedforward, feedback, or simultaneous/volume-conduction-like activation.

pipeline_review.reviewer: Claude (separate session, code-review only, no edits to jnwb/onset_fitting.py or scripts/fit_class_onset_latency.py)
pipeline_review.detail: Causal (forward-only) smoothing matches the project's documented PSTH convention (omission-figures skill: tau_ms=30 default). Onset fit is causality-bounded by construction (t0 cannot leave [0, window_end] regardless of what an unconstrained fit would report), mirroring the existing cluster-permutation onset search's own causal restriction. Self-tested on synthetic PSTHs (including a case specifically stress-testing the grid-search-then-refine fix for a t0/tau degeneracy the author found and fixed on real data 2026-08-15) before being trusted on real data, per this project's established self-test precedent. bootstrap_area_class already excludes r2<0.3 / non-converged fits from area-level onset estimates before the hierarchy test sees them -- correctly reasoned as 'a degenerate near-zero-amplitude fit parks t0 near a bound with a flat residual, not a real onset.'

O+.note: O++ already included by construction (omission_class in {O+,O++}) -- pooling did not need to be 'tried', it is structural. Still underpowered.

new_finding_this_session.what: A boundary-pinning failure mode distinct from the pipeline's existing r2/converged gate: cells with r2>=0.3 and converged=True can still have t0 pinned near 0ms AND tau pinned near its lower bound (1.0ms) simultaneously -- the signature of a step+exponential model being forced (by the causality bound t0>=0) to compress a pre-existing ramp (activity already rising before the window opens) into the earliest allowed point and fastest allowed time constant, rather than reporting no clean post-t0 onset. This is a real, converged fit and not evidence of a genuine <1ms neural onset.
new_finding_this_session.method: scripts/diagnose_onset_hierarchy_boundary_pinning.py (new file, reads cell_fits.csv only, no edits to the pipeline). Flag: gate-passing cell (r2>=0.3, converged) with t0<1.0ms AND tau<=1.01ms.

headline_numbers.S+: 1/38 gate-passing cells pinned (2.6%, PFC only) -- the positive-control class is essentially clean, which strengthens confidence in its null result (this is not an artifact-driven flat line)
headline_numbers.omnibus: 13/63 gate-passing cells pinned (20.6%), concentrated in FEF (4/10, 40%), TEO (4/8, 50%), V3a/d (2/7, 29%), MST (1/4, 25%), PFC (2/12, 17%) -- these are largely the same areas whose area-level onset lands near 0ms in the receipt's own flag list, so the omnibus H3-superposition verdict is currently confounded by this artifact in several areas, not purely a biological simultaneity finding
headline_numbers.S-_and_O-: every gate-passing S-/O- cell in FEF-S-(2/2), PFC-S-(3/3), PFC-O-(4/4), V3a/d-O-(1/1) is 100% pinned -- the sparse S-/O- results that do exist are not merely underpowered, they are entirely artifact, and should not be read as preliminary evidence of anything

new_finding_this_session.not_yet_done: Root cause not confirmed by inspecting raw PSTH shapes directly (e.g. plotting a pinned cell's rate trace against a longer pre-window than the fit currently uses, S_WIN_MS=(-100,400)/O_WIN_MS=(-100,600), to visually confirm pre-onset ramping). The model-misspecification explanation is the best-supported hypothesis given the t0+tau co-pinning pattern, not yet independently verified against raw spike data.

recommendation: Do not cite the omnibus H1/H2/H3 verdict, or any S-/O- onset number, in a manuscript claim yet. S+ is the one class currently trustworthy at face value (real null, not artifact-driven). Before the omnibus/O+/O- test can be trusted: (1) add a boundary-pinning flag to fit_class_onset_latency.py's own output (parallel to its existing MIN_VISUAL_LATENCY_MS flag) so a future run self-reports this rather than requiring a separate diagnostic pass; (2) consider widening the pre-onset baseline/fit window to let a pre-existing ramp be visible to the model instead of truncated at the causality bound, if a wider window remains scientifically defensible for this alignment; (3) get more sessions/units before the O+/O-/S- classes can support a per-area comparison at all -- this is a data-volume problem, not something the fitting method can solve.
